summary: Hawaii-only chatbot compliance is a tiny, unquantified market with no sign anyone will pay, and its valuable parts (suicide detection, guardian portal) are liability-heavy and not weekend builds. The M1 banner is trivial and proves nothing about demand.

demand.evidence: Only a statute and two vendor case studies (Akia, Romaix) exist; the $29/month price is a guess. No payer, no outreach, and Act 248's scope for ordinary customer-service bots is unconfirmed.

statusQuo.evidence: Status quo is a disclaimer plus a 988 link, or DIY in 20-60 hours; generic widgets (Disclosed €19, Normis free) exist. Attestly's $500-2,000 is for broad platforms, not proof of willingness to pay here.

specificity.evidence: Buyer is a category (operators of conversational AI in Hawaii). No named person, role or consequence; the named firms are vendors, not customers.

wedge.evidence: Eight features across seven milestones. M1 is a disclaimer banner nobody pays for; the paid parts are liability-heavy. The honest wedge is a free checklist plus snippet and report template.

futureFit.evidence: More state chatbot laws make only a multi-state version viable, which is a different, crowded idea. A Hawaii-only product depends on one statute that may change.

premises: Act 248 creates real obligations for ordinary Hawaiian chatbot operators: unsupported, scope looks narrower
Operators will pay about $29/month instead of adding a disclaimer themselves: a guess
A widget can detect suicide ideation reliably enough to lean on legally: doubtful
The Hawaii market is big enough: no operator count in the research
A script tag can see chat content: it can't without an SDK or proxy integration
alternatives: Free static page: Act 248 checklist, disclosure snippet and DOH report template (S, tests interest)
Extend permitly/vendorfile into a multi-state chatbot-law tracker with an evidence log
Multi-state chatbot-safety SDK with audit logs (XL, crowded, high liability): not recommended
wedge: Act 248 checklist plus audit-log and annual-report generator for companion-style chatbot operators, with no detection or classifier claims.

feasibility.notes: Static JS widget on Vercel Hobby with localStorage; a Playwright test of the three M1 exit criteria. It proves the banner works, not demand. M2-M5 need NLP/moderation APIs and auth, which breaks zero cost and weekend scope.

risks: Liability for crisis-handling and compliance claims from a keyword list
Statute scope unclear and may be amended or challenged
Operators can comply with a prompt change and a disclaimer
Guardian portal needs age and parent verification a widget can't do
killCriteria: Drop it if after two weeks of a free checklist page there are fewer than 50 relevant visitors, fewer than 3 operators ask for the paid tool, or no operator confirms Act 248 applies to them.
